recursion_observatory.name: Recursion Observatory
recursion_observatory.description: Four recursions held at one rung on four plinths, ordered by D = log(N)/log(s): Cantor 0.63, Koch 1.26, Sierpinski 2.32, Menger 2.73. Each plaque etches the branching factor, the dimension, how many rungs that artifact's own ladder declares, and which of two walls ends it.
recursion_observatory.qfep_connection: F-compression at its limit. Each of these four rules is a complete description of an endless object in one line, which is the highest compression ratio anything in this corpus reaches. What the row exhibits is the part the compression cannot carry: a rule is scale-free and a drawing is not, so every one of them stops, and the rung it stops on is set by the width of the pen or by the instance budget rather than by the mathematics. The residue that will not compress is the apparatus.
recursion_observatory.relationships: Synthesis of [[cantor_set]], [[koch_curve_3d]], [[sierpinski_pyramid]] and [[menger_sponge]] — the four artifacts that share the `tick` word. WHAT THEY LEARNED SEPARATELY: [[cantor_set]] reaches 5 rungs and 32 bars, and stops because a sixth row is 12 mm of segment against its own bar's 300 mm depth. [[koch_curve_3d]] declares 3 rungs and SKIPS n=3, because the bump added at generation n has amplitude 0.076 m against a drawing tube of radius 0.2 m, and iterations 3, 4, 5 and 6 measured as one photograph. [[sierpinski_pyramid]] declares 5 rungs and stops on instance count at the 3125 its @identity names — and it also refused [[cantor_set]]'s `removal` word, because its children's volumes interpenetrate and there is no complement to draw. [[menger_sponge]] declares 3, because each tick multiplies the cube count by 20 and a fourth rung would be 160,000. WHAT ONLY THE ROW CAN SAY: held side by side the ladders run 5, 3, 5, 3 against branching factors 2, 4, 5, 20, and they are NOT ordered by the branching factor. Sierpinski branches faster than Koch and reaches two more rungs. What ends a ladder is whichever wall arrives first — COUNT, where N^n exceeds what can be instanced, or THICKNESS, where extent/s^n falls under the pen that draws it — and which wall that is depends on how the artifact is drawn, not on the rule. None of the four is replaced or moved: each keeps its own drawing here (Cantor its hue-per-level law, Koch its emissive line and its arch head), and all four stay placed in their own maps.

dna.default: tick=fine — the top of this row's three rungs, and the only value at which the whole claim is on show at once: at n=3 Cantor and Sierpinski are on rung 3 of a 5-rung ladder and still climbing, Koch is on the last rung its own file will draw, and the Menger plinth is HELD at n=2 with its plaque saying so, because its third rung is 8000 leaves. `once` and `coarse` are the same row earlier. Nothing is preserved by this choice and nothing can be regressed by it — this artifact has no shipped placements, so the default is a free design choice, and this is the strongest single reading.
dna.was: synthesized from cantor_set, koch_curve_3d, sierpinski_pyramid and menger_sponge — four separate promotions, each of which declared `tick`, stopped its ladder at a different rung, and wrote the reason into its own registry note where no one can stand in front of it.
dna.kin: `tick` is the word all four sources share, and the only word all four share, so it is the only word this row takes. THREE RUNGS: once | coarse | fine, character for character the list menger_sponge and koch_curve_3d carry, and the first three of cantor_set's and sierpinski_pyramid's five. Three is the INTERSECTION and not a convenience — it is the deepest rung every member can honestly be shown at, and declaring `dense` and `limit` would be menger_sponge's own example_8_4 fault one level up: rungs that exist in the enum and that two of the four members cannot reach. ONE DIFFERENCE FROM THE SOURCES' USE OF THE WORD, deliberate and on the record: here `tick` names the RULE-APPLICATION COUNT n and nothing else, matched across the four, because n is the only quantity comparable between a thirds rule and a 3x3x3 lattice. koch_curve_3d's own `fine` is n=4, its table skipping 3 because 3 and 4 measured as one photograph at its shipped 0.2 m line width; this row's third rung is n=3 for everybody, and it can show n=3 on Koch because it draws with a 0.012 m segment against a 1.02 m span rather than 0.2 m against 4.71 m. The wall is a property of the drawing, which is the row's whole thesis, so moving it is allowed as long as it is said out loud.
dna.note: Four plinths on one base, ordered left to right by D — 0.63, 1.26, 2.32, 2.73 — with a dimension rail along the front running 0 to 3 and a marker under each member's true D. The plinths are evenly spaced and the markers are not: Sierpinski and Menger are close neighbours in dimension while Cantor sits below one, and the mismatch between even spacing and true dimension is the row's second reading. Each plaque carries four lines: the name; N, s and D; how many rungs that artifact's own ladder declares and which wall ends it; and the rung this row holds it at, with the leaf count. THE LADDER LENGTHS ARE READ, NOT TYPED — `LADDER n RUNGS` is TICK_LEVELS.size() off each source's own script through a preload, which is slot_machine's pattern, so the four cannot drift from what this row claims about them. THE FOUR RULES ARE DRAWN HERE, NOT INSTANCED: cantor_set grows a row every 2 s and drops its bars with unfrozen RigidBody3D, menger_sponge subdivides on a 1 s clock and every leaf it makes is a cube_scene carrying a StaticBody3D and a CollisionShape3D, and both needed dna.fixture build_mode=instant before a still could see them at all. A row of four cannot afford four fixtures and four hundred colliders, so each rule is re-implemented as plain MeshInstance3D boxes out of the source's own arithmetic: Cantor's thirds and its Color.from_hsv(level/max_iterations, 0.8, 0.9) hue law, Koch's four-point iteration and its `head = arch` mapping line for line, Menger's 3x3x3 lattice. Menger's keep set is DERIVED rather than copied — drop every sub-cube with two or more centre coordinates — and that rule was checked against the source's keep_positions table and reproduces it exactly, removing 4, 10, 12, 13, 14, 16 and 22. The lattice index is built from three nested loops because the source computed it as i % 3, (i / 3) % 3 and i / 9.0, and that last float divide is the one character that meant the shipped object was not a Menger sponge.
dna.finding: SIERPINSKI_PYRAMID BRANCHES BY SIX, NOT FIVE, AND ITS OWN MEASUREMENT PROVES IT. SierpinskiPyramid.gd's _recursive_build makes SIX recursive calls: a `# Top` at pos + (0, half_size, 0) on line 109, a second `# Top` at pos + (0, offset, 0) on line 174 where offset = half_size / 2, and then the four bottoms. Its @identity says 'pyramid(depth) = 5 * pyramid(depth-1)', its DNA note says 'each increment multiplies complexity by 5, from 5 cubes to 3125', and its registry entry says 'all 625 leaves land on the same coordinates' and 'limit builds 3125 static bodies where the shipped depth builds 625'. Re-implemented in Python from the file and run at every depth, the six-call recursion gives 6, 36, 216, 1296, 7776 leaves and an AABB at depth 4 of 8.50 x 12.25 x 8.50 with centre y 1.88 — which is that entry's own measured aabb_size and aabb_center, to the centimetre. The five-child rule gives 8.50 x 8.50 x 8.50 with centre y 0.00, and does not. So the shipped depth builds 1296 cube_scene instances rather than 625, and the declared `limit` rung builds 7776 static bodies rather than 3125 — 2.5x the frame that entry's still_note already flagged as the one that could trip the 16-second watchdog, and its COUNT wall arrives correspondingly sooner than it says. NOT REPAIRED HERE: the fix changes what six live placements draw, which is that artifact's own pass and not a synthesis's business. This row draws the rule the artifact ARGUES — five copies at half scale, apex plus four base corners — and etches that. A SECOND, SMALLER MISMATCH in the same entry: its `packing` note reads 'the Sierpinski tetrahedron has Hausdorff dimension exactly 2', which is the FOUR-child tetrix. A five-child square-based pyramid at half scale has D = log 5 / log 2 = 2.3219, and 2.32 is the number on the plinth.
dna.declines:
`removal` REFUSED. cantor_set and menger_sponge share it (gone | ghost | scar) and it is the obvious second axis to reach for — and it fits only two of the four members. sierpinski_pyramid already refused it and was right to, its children's bounding volumes interpenetrating so that there is no complement to draw; and koch_curve_3d has no complement at all, because the Koch rule takes the middle third and hands back two sides of a triangle, so the drawn figure is continuous and nothing anywhere is missing from it. Declaring `removal` across this row would be folding_past's fault exactly — taking a word without its answers on half the objects it is applied to.

`packing` REFUSED for the opposite reason: it is applicable everywhere and means a different thing in each place. On sierpinski_pyramid the leaf is an atom sitting on a lattice cell of known spacing, and shrinking it withdraws a claim about MEASURE the drawing was making by accident. On Cantor the surviving segment IS the set — shrinking it does not reveal a point cloud, it draws a different fractal. Same word, two questions.

A TEXT AXIS REFUSED ON A MEASUREMENT rather than on taste. `evidence`, the corpus's most-shared word, would suit an observatory well — how much of its own arithmetic the apparatus shows — and it cannot be photographed here. The five plaques and the rail caption together cover roughly 0.30 m2 of a 6.36 m fit-by-diagonal frame, about 0.7% of it, and only a fraction of that is glyph. The strongest possible swap of every word on the object lands under the 2% bite floor, so declaring it would ship a finished-looking experiment that answers nothing, which is info_board's fault.

NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED, and this is worth saying rather than leaving blank: there is no clock, no RigidBody3D, no @tool path and no randf() in the file, so _ready lays the finished row out in one frame and it never moves again. Both cantor_set and menger_sponge needed dna.fixture build_mode=instant before any axis of theirs was visible at all; this one needs nothing supplied.
dna.still_note:
`tick` changes three plinths of four and DELIBERATELY LEAVES THE FOURTH ALONE between coarse and fine. That identity is the exhibit and not a fault: Menger's third rung is 8000 leaves, so the row holds it at n=2 and its plaque reads HELD - n=3 IS 8000. An INERT reading of that quadrant is the finding arriving on schedule.

THE FRAME NUMBER WILL LOOK THIN AND THE FOCUS NUMBER WILL NOT, and the gap is geometric. Estimated by mirroring this file's constants in Python and rasterising a front elevation at 1400 px across the fit-by-diagonal frame with every box filled and outlined — a boolean silhouette XOR is the WRONG metric for this family and reports 0.73% for a frame that changes wholesale, because self-similarity is exactly the claim that the outline does not change:

    n=1 -> n=2    frame 1.34%    focus (hottest 5%) 26.7%
    n=2 -> n=3    frame 0.59%    focus (hottest 5%) 11.9%
    n=1 -> n=3    frame 1.83%    focus (hottest 5%) 36.7%

So the axis clears the 3% focus floor by 4x at its weakest step and clears 2% of frame at no step at all. THAT IS DILUTION, the known trap: the changing part is four small densely textured volumes inside a 5.90 m row, and the subject covers 10-12% of frame at every rung. Crop-recheck per plinth before believing anything measured frame-wide. These are estimates from an orthographic elevation and not the bench, which is perspective from a raised angle; its numbers will differ.

The union AABB is 5.90 x 1.96 x 1.34 m and is IDENTICAL at all three rungs, because every fractal's extent is held constant while its texture changes — so the fixed camera fits all three variants equally and no value is photographed from further away. Element count is about 55, 471 and 627 meshes at once, coarse and fine, every one a plain MeshInstance3D with no collision and no MultiMesh, well inside the 3200 budget; the 400 Menger leaves are the bulk of it at both coarse and fine. dna.framing is deliberately NOT declared: the diagonal is 6.36 m against a width of 5.90 m, an inflation of 8%, so fit-by-diagonal is very nearly fit-by-width here and a framing below 1.0 would crop the end plinths.
